content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"Yes: it calls Matthew 1:20 UNDERDETERMINED on the basis that the challenger reads it as covenant presence while the defender reads it as physical source, treating the verse's two senses as open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open — I weighed (1) the judge treats Matthew 1:20's covenant-presence and physical-source readings as two senses leaving it underdetermined, which K-S2 forbids, versus (2) the judge merely notes each side's answer without saying the verse carries both senses, so K-S2 might not reach it.","why":"K-S2 forbids leaving a verse with two senses open, since both senses stand, so the underdetermined label breaches the rule."}
